MacPherson established a correspondence between the cohomology of the space of smooth semistable curves and the mixed Hodge structure of the diagonal of a complex manifold. We aim to extend this correspondence to a more general setting, where semi-stability is defined by a rational function on the curves, under specific conditions that ensure semistability behaves well. This extension is significant as it enables the use of the decomposition of the integral cohomology of the space of semistable curves to break down the diagonal of a compact complex manifold. This, in turn, provides a novel method to assign the diagonal's sphericity to a component of the space of semistable curves, thereby defining a point in the third homology sphere module of the manifold.
